tasks.script_en: Hi, Anna. Our English class is not at nine today. It starts at ten thirty in room twelve.
tasks.question_en: When does the English class start?
tasks.explanation_ru: Говорящий исправляет первое время: занятие начинается at ten thirty, то есть в 10:30.

tasks.script_en: I need milk, bread, and two apples. I will go to the grocery store after work and then cook dinner.
tasks.question_en: What is the speaker mainly talking about?
options: Buying food
Going to a restaurant
Starting a new job
Making breakfast
tasks.explanation_ru: Главная мысль — покупка продуктов: перечислены milk, bread, apples и поход в grocery store.

tasks.script_en: Every morning I take a shower, eat some eggs, and walk to the bus stop. I drink coffee at the office.
tasks.question_en: What does the speaker do after breakfast?
options: Takes a shower
Walks to the bus stop
Drinks coffee at home
Goes back to bed
tasks.explanation_ru: После eat some eggs идёт walk to the bus stop; кофе человек пьёт уже в офисе.

tasks.script_en: I want to get my laptop, but the office is dark and the front door is locked. It is seven o'clock on Sunday morning.
tasks.question_en: Why can't the speaker get in?
options: The office is closed on Sunday
There is no electricity in the building
The front door is broken
It is too late in the evening
tasks.explanation_ru: Человек пришёл за ноутбуком, но дверь заперта (locked), внутри темно, а на часах seven o'clock on Sunday morning — в выходной офис закрыт. Дверь не сломана, а заперта; темно, потому что внутри никого нет, об электричестве ничего не сказано; и сейчас утро, а не вечер.

tasks.script_en: This coffee smells great, but it is much too sweet for me. Next time I will order it without sugar.
tasks.question_en: How does the speaker feel about the coffee?
options: Likes everything and will order the same again
Likes the smell, but not the taste
Likes the taste, but not the smell
Does not like it and will not order it again
tasks.explanation_ru: Запах говорящий хвалит (smells great), а вкус нет: кофе much too sweet. Отказываться от него он не собирается — в следующий раз закажет without sugar.

tasks.script_en:
Emma: Excuse me, how much is this blue T-shirt?
Sam: It's fifteen dollars. The white one is twelve.
Emma: OK, I like the blue one. Do you have it in medium?
Sam: Yes, here you go.
tasks.question_en: How much is the blue T-shirt?
options: Twelve dollars
Fifteen dollars
Fifty dollars
Sixteen dollars
tasks.explanation_ru: Продавец называет цену синей футболки: It's fifteen dollars. Twelve — цена белой, а fifteen легко спутать с fifty: в fifteen ударение падает на второй слог.

tasks.script_en:
Lily: Hi, Mom! Are you free on Saturday?
Anna: Yes, I think so. Why?
Lily: It's Ben's birthday. We're having a small party at our place at two. Can you come?
Anna: Of course! I'll bring a cake.
tasks.question_en: What is the phone call mainly about?
options: Asking Mom to bring a birthday cake
Inviting Mom to a birthday party
Planning a party at Mom's place
Asking Mom about her Saturday plans
tasks.explanation_ru: Лили звонит, чтобы позвать маму на день рождения Бена: We're having a small party... Can you come? Торт мама предлагает принести сама (I'll bring a cake), а праздник будет у Лили — at our place.

tasks.script_en: Hi, it's Kate. Let's meet at the train station tomorrow at ten. First, we'll visit the art museum. Then we'll have lunch in the park. After lunch, we can go shopping, OK? See you!
tasks.question_en: What will they do right after the museum?
options: Go shopping
Have lunch in the park
Go back to the station
Have coffee at home
tasks.explanation_ru: Порядок такой: встреча на вокзале → музей → Then we'll have lunch in the park → After lunch, we can go shopping. Сразу после музея — обед в парке, магазины потом.

tasks.script_en:
Jack: Good evening. A table for two, please.
Nina: Sure. Inside or by the window?
Jack: By the window, please. And can we see the menu?
Nina: Here you are. Today's soup is tomato.
tasks.question_en: Where are Jack and Nina?
options: On a train
In a restaurant
In a food store
At a friend's home
tasks.explanation_ru: Место прямо не названо, но A table for two, please, просьба показать menu и Today's soup is tomato — это ресторан. Место у окна бывает и в поезде, но столик на двоих и суп дня там не предлагают.

tasks.script_en: I love my new apartment. It's small, but the kitchen is big and bright. The only problem is the noise. The street is very busy at night. But I'm really happy here.
tasks.question_en: How does the speaker feel about the new apartment?
options: Happy, but the street is noisy
Unhappy, because it is too small
Happy, but the kitchen is too small
Unhappy, and wants to move
tasks.explanation_ru: Говорящий доволен: I love my new apartment и I'm really happy here. Минус один — шум: The only problem is the noise. Маленькая сама квартира, а кухня как раз big and bright; переезжать он не собирается.

tasks.script_en: Attention, please. The train to Boston will leave at eleven fifteen from platform six, not platform four. It is running ten minutes late.
tasks.question_en: Which platform will the train leave from?
options: Platform four
Platform five
Platform six
Platform ten
tasks.explanation_ru: Объявление специально противопоставляет from platform six, not platform four.

tasks.script_en: I usually work at the office, but today I am staying home. A repair person is coming to fix my kitchen sink, so I will join all meetings online.
tasks.question_en: What is the speaker mainly telling the team?
options: The speaker is sick and cannot come to today's meetings
The speaker is staying home today but will join the meetings
A repair person is coming to fix the kitchen in the office
Today's meetings are moving online for the whole team
tasks.explanation_ru: Главное сообщение: сегодня человек работает из дома (today I am staying home), но на всех встречах будет онлайн (I will join all meetings online). Мастер придёт к нему домой чинить раковину, а онлайн встречи только для него, а не для всей команды.

tasks.script_en: First, check that all the tests are green. Then ask Maria to review the change. After she approves it, you can deploy the new version.
tasks.question_en: What should happen immediately before deployment?
options: Checking that the tests are green
Getting Maria's approval
Asking Maria to review the change
Asking Maria to deploy
tasks.explanation_ru: Порядок такой: tests are green → ask Maria to review → she approves → deploy. Непосредственно перед deploy стоит её одобрение; просьба о ревью идёт раньше, а выкатывает версию сам слушатель, а не Maria.

tasks.script_en: Leo's chair is empty, and he sent me a photo from the airport this morning. He said he would be back in the office next Monday.
tasks.question_en: Why is Leo's chair empty?
options: He is on a trip
He is in another meeting
He is having lunch
He is sick at home
tasks.explanation_ru: Фото из аэропорта и возвращение в офис только в следующий понедельник указывают на поездку, а не на встречу, обед или болезнь.

tasks.script_en: The new app looks cleaner, and the search is faster. I still cannot find the settings easily, but overall this update is much better than the old version.
tasks.question_en: What is the speaker's overall opinion?
options: Mostly positive
Completely negative
Not interested
The old and new versions are identical
tasks.explanation_ru: Есть один минус со settings, но overall и much better показывают в целом положительную оценку.

tasks.script_en: Attention, please. Passengers on flight three twenty to Denver, your flight is delayed by forty minutes because of snow. The new departure time is five fifty. Please stay near gate twelve. We're sorry for the delay, and thank you for your patience.
tasks.question_en: What is the new departure time?
tasks.explanation_ru: Новое время названо прямо: The new departure time is five fifty — 5:50. Three twenty — номер рейса, forty minutes — длительность задержки, а fifty легко спутать с fifteen.

tasks.script_en:
Ella: Hi, I'd like something for a sore throat, please.
Ron: Sure. Do you have a fever too?
Ella: No, but I've had a bad cough since Monday.
Ron: OK, try this syrup twice a day. If you don't feel better in three days, see a doctor.
tasks.question_en: What is the conversation mainly about?
options: Making an appointment with a doctor
Getting medicine for a throat and cough
Buying medicine to bring down a fever
Asking when the pharmacy opens on Monday
tasks.explanation_ru: Элла просит something for a sore throat, рассказывает про кашель, и ей советуют сироп twice a day. К врачу идти нужно, только если через три дня не станет лучше; температуры у неё нет (No), а Monday — день, когда начался кашель.

tasks.script_en:
Paul: Excuse me, how do I get to the post office?
Maya: Go straight to the bank, then turn left. Walk past the park, and it's on your right, next to a small café.
Paul: So, left at the bank, then past the park?
Maya: That's right. It's about five minutes.
tasks.question_en: What will Paul walk past right after he turns left?
options: The bank
The park
A small café
The post office
tasks.explanation_ru: Маршрут: straight to the bank → turn left → Walk past the park → почта справа, рядом с кафе. После поворота Пол проходит мимо парка; банк остаётся до поворота, а кафе стоит уже у самой почты.

tasks.script_en: Hi, it's Greg from next door. I found a little brown dog in my backyard this morning. It has a red collar with your phone number on it. Don't worry, it's fine, and it's eating now. Please call me when you get home.
tasks.question_en: What has probably happened?
options: The listener's dog got out of the house
Greg has lost his own dog
The dog got hurt in Greg's backyard
Greg wants to give the listener a dog
tasks.explanation_ru: Прямо это не сказано, но на ошейнике номер телефона слушателя (your phone number), а нашлась собака у соседа — значит, это собака слушателя и она сбежала из дома. С ней всё в порядке (it's fine), а свою собаку Грег не терял.

tasks.script_en:
Kim: So, how was the movie last night? Everybody's talking about it.
Dan: Well, the actors were great, but it was way too long. Almost three hours!
Kim: Would you see it again?
Dan: Hmm, maybe at home, but not at the movie theater.
tasks.question_en: What does Dan think of the movie?
options: He loved it and wants to see it again soon
He liked the actors but found it too long
He didn't like the actors but liked the story
He thought it was boring from start to end
tasks.explanation_ru: Дэн хвалит актёров (the actors were great), но жалуется на длину: way too long. Almost three hours! Пересмотреть он готов разве что дома (maybe at home), а не в кинотеатре.

tasks.script_en: We originally promised the report by Thursday afternoon. Since the finance team cannot send its figures until Thursday evening, I have agreed with the client to deliver the final version before noon on Friday.
tasks.question_en: What is the new deadline for the final report?
options: Thursday morning
Thursday afternoon
Thursday evening
Friday before noon
tasks.explanation_ru: Старый срок был Thursday afternoon, а согласованный новый — before noon on Friday.

tasks.script_en: Yesterday's outage was not caused by the new release. One of our database certificates had expired, so the service could not connect after its scheduled restart. We renewed the certificate and added an automatic warning for next time.
tasks.question_en: What is the main purpose of this message?
options: To report that yesterday's outage was caused by the new release
To explain the real cause of the outage and its fix
To announce a scheduled restart of the database service
To warn the team that more certificates will expire soon
tasks.explanation_ru: Сообщение объясняет настоящую причину outage — истёк сертификат базы, — сделанное исправление и новое предупреждение на будущее. Новый релиз прямо назван невиновным, а restart упомянут как момент сбоя, а не как анонс.

tasks.script_en: Please write down the two changes the customer requested and send the notes to the team. Once everyone has checked them, create the tickets, but do not estimate the work until tomorrow's planning meeting.
tasks.question_en: What should the listener do after the team checks the notes?
options: Create the tickets
Estimate the work
Call the customer again
Start coding immediately
tasks.explanation_ru: После проверки заметок нужно create the tickets; оценивать работу просят только на завтрашнем planning.

tasks.script_en: Sam did not say much during the first ten minutes, but his answers became detailed when we discussed real production problems. He also asked thoughtful questions about monitoring and support duties.
tasks.question_en: What can be inferred about Sam?
options: He has little experience with production systems
He became more comfortable as the interview went on
He knows monitoring better than coding
He is more interested in support than in development
tasks.explanation_ru: Сначала Sam говорил мало, а потом стал подробно отвечать о реальных production problems и задавать продуманные вопросы — он освоился. Monitoring и support он лишь упомянул в своих вопросах; сравнения с кодом или разработкой в записи нет.

tasks.script_en: I understand why we added a second approval, and it has already caught two serious mistakes. However, waiting a full day for every small documentation change feels unnecessary. I think we should keep the rule only for code changes.
tasks.question_en: What does the speaker think about the new process?
options: It is useful but should cover only documentation changes
It is useful but applied too broadly
It slows everyone down and has caught nothing serious
It is fine as it is, but reviews should be faster
tasks.explanation_ru: Второй approval уже поймал две серьёзные ошибки, но ждать сутки ради мелкой правки документации говорящий считает лишним и предлагает оставить правило только для code changes — то есть сузить его, а не ускорить.

tasks.script_en:
Olivia: Hi, I have a reservation under Martinez, for two nights.
Jake: Let me check. Yes, here it is. You're in room four oh six, on the fourth floor.
Olivia: Great. And what time is breakfast?
Jake: On weekdays, it's from six thirty to ten, but on weekends it starts at seven.
Olivia: And tomorrow's Saturday, right?
Jake: That's right.
tasks.question_en: What time does breakfast start tomorrow?
tasks.explanation_ru: Завтра суббота (tomorrow's Saturday), а on weekends it starts at seven — в 7:00. С 6:30 завтрак начинается только по будням, а ten — время, когда он заканчивается.

tasks.script_en: Good morning, this is City Radio with your local news. Starting next month, the city's bike-sharing program is expanding to the east side, with thirty new stations. Rides under thirty minutes will stay free for anyone with a city card, and visitors will be able to pay by phone. The mayor says the goal is to cut traffic downtown, especially during rush hour.
tasks.question_en: What is the news story mainly about?
options: Free bus rides for people with a city card
The bike-sharing program growing to a new area
A new app that lets visitors pay by phone
The mayor's plan to close downtown to cars
tasks.explanation_ru: Главная новость — расширение велопроката: the city's bike-sharing program is expanding to the east side, with thirty new stations. Бесплатные поездки по city card и оплата по телефону — детали, а закрывать центр для машин никто не собирается: мэр хочет лишь cut traffic.

tasks.script_en:
Sophie: Mom, I'm making your pancakes, but I forgot the order.
Linda: OK. Mix the flour, sugar, and salt first. Then add the milk and eggs.
Sophie: And the butter? Do I just put it in the pan?
Linda: No, melt it and add it to the batter at the end. Then let it rest for ten minutes before you cook anything.
Sophie: Got it. Rest, then cook.
Linda: Exactly.
tasks.question_en: What should Sophie do right after adding the milk and eggs?
options: Put butter in the pan
Add the melted butter
Let the batter rest
Start cooking the pancakes
tasks.explanation_ru: Порядок: flour, sugar, salt → milk and eggs → растопленное масло at the end → rest for ten minutes → жарить. Масло не кладут на сковороду (No, melt it), а отдыхать тесто оставляют уже после масла.

tasks.script_en:
Tyler: Hey, are you still coming to the game tonight?
Megan: I'd love to, but have you looked outside?
Tyler: Oh. Yeah, it's really coming down. Do you think they'll play?
Megan: Last time it was like this, they waited two hours and then sent everyone home. I'll watch it on TV, if they play at all.
Tyler: Fair enough. I'm still going. I've got a good umbrella.
tasks.question_en: What does Megan expect to happen tonight?
options: The game will be delayed or canceled
The game will start two hours early
Tyler will decide to stay at home
The game won't be shown on TV
tasks.explanation_ru: Прямо Меган этого не говорит, но вспоминает, что в прошлый раз в такую погоду they waited two hours and then sent everyone home, и добавляет if they play at all — она ждёт задержки или отмены. Матч она собирается смотреть по телевизору, а Тайлер всё равно пойдёт.

tasks.script_en: I've been going to the new gym on Pine Street for a month now. The equipment's brand-new, and the staff are really friendly. But honestly, for eighty dollars a month, I expected longer hours. It closes at nine, which is too early for me. I'll probably stay until my contract ends, and then I'll look for something cheaper.
tasks.question_en: How does the speaker feel about the gym?
options: Happy with it and planning to stay for years
Likes it but feels it isn't worth the price
Dislikes the staff but likes the equipment
Likes the hours but not the equipment
tasks.explanation_ru: Оборудование и персонал говорящий хвалит (brand-new, really friendly), но за eighty dollars a month ждал более долгих часов работы и после окончания контракта поищет something cheaper — цена кажется ему завышенной.

tasks.script_en: Our cloud bill rose by eighteen percent in the first quarter, mainly because the analytics cluster was running overnight. Turning it off outside business hours should save about twelve thousand dollars a month, while the planned storage change will save another three thousand.
tasks.question_en: How much should the storage change save each month?
options: Three thousand dollars
Twelve thousand dollars
Fifteen thousand dollars
Eighteen thousand dollars
tasks.explanation_ru: Twelve thousand относится к отключению кластера, а storage change даст another three thousand.

tasks.script_en: Moving every customer at once would shorten the project, but a single unnoticed compatibility issue could affect the entire platform. We will therefore start with internal accounts, monitor them for two weeks, and expand the migration only if the error rate remains stable.
tasks.question_en: Which approach has the team chosen?
options: Moving every customer at once to finish sooner
Starting with internal accounts and expanding if errors stay stable
Migrating only internal accounts and stopping there
Moving all customers at once, then monitoring for two weeks
tasks.explanation_ru: Одновременный переезд сократил бы проект, но рискован, поэтому команда начнёт с internal accounts, понаблюдает две недели и расширит миграцию, только если error rate останется стабильным. Две недели наблюдения относятся к внутренним аккаунтам, а не ко всем клиентам.

tasks.script_en: Before you leave, update the incident guide and walk Nina through the unresolved payment issue. She will take over the support rotation once she has access to the dashboard, so ask security to grant that access before arranging the handover call.
tasks.question_en: What must happen before the handover call is arranged?
options: The payment issue must be resolved
Nina must receive dashboard access
The support rotation must end
The incident guide must be deleted
tasks.explanation_ru: Прямо сказано grant that access before arranging the handover call.

tasks.script_en: So, quick update on Friday's launch. Marketing has already prepared the announcement, and the feature passed all functional tests on Tuesday. Well, technically Wednesday morning, after the last fix went in. On paper, everything's green. Still, the team lead asked everyone to keep Friday evening free and not to plan any trips that weekend. She's also requested an extra rollback rehearsal on Thursday, and she wants support to have instructions for the old version ready, just in case. So, you know, don't book anything yet.
tasks.question_en: What is the team lead probably concerned about?
options: Marketing announcing the feature too early
Problems in production after the launch
The feature failing its functional tests
The announcement not being ready in time
tasks.explanation_ru: Функциональные тесты пройдены и анонс готов, но тимлид просит держать свободными вечер пятницы и выходные, заказывает extra rollback rehearsal и инструкции к старой версии для поддержки just in case — она опасается проблем в эксплуатации после запуска. О спешке маркетинга в записи ничего нет.

tasks.script_en: The demo was polished, and I can see why the sales team liked it. Yet every difficult question was answered with a promise about the next release, while the contract requires a three-year commitment. I would not sign anything until we speak to existing customers.
tasks.question_en: How does the speaker feel about the vendor?
options: Impressed by the demo and ready to sign after the next release
Impressed by the demo but doubtful about the vendor's promises
Unimpressed by the demo but confident in the vendor's roadmap
Doubtful about the demo but happy with a three-year contract
tasks.explanation_ru: Демо говорящий хвалит (polished), но на каждый трудный вопрос звучало обещание про next release, а контракт требует трёх лет — поэтому он ничего не подпишет, пока не поговорит с existing customers. Ждать следующего релиза он не предлагает.

tasks.script_en:
Rachel: Hi, I'm calling about the two-bedroom on Maple Avenue. Is it still available?
Victor: It is. Rent's eighteen hundred a month, and that includes water and trash, but not electricity.
Rachel: OK. And what about the deposit?
Victor: It's one month's rent, so eighteen hundred. Oh, wait, sorry, for this unit it's actually fifteen hundred, since it hasn't been renovated yet.
Rachel: Got it. And pets? I've got a cat.
Victor: Cats are fine, but there's a fifty-dollar monthly pet fee.
tasks.question_en: How much is the deposit for this apartment?
tasks.explanation_ru: Сначала Виктор называет залог в размере месячной аренды (eighteen hundred), но тут же поправляется: for this unit it's actually fifteen hundred — $1,500. $1,800 — сама аренда, а $50 — ежемесячная плата за питомца.

tasks.script_en: Welcome back to Healthy Habits. So, today's question comes from a listener who, um, can't fall asleep before two in the morning. Now, most people blame their phones, and, well, screens do play a part. But the research we looked at, or most of it anyway, points somewhere else: to irregular schedules. If you go to bed at eleven on weekdays and at two or three on weekends, your body never really knows when night is. So before you buy another sleep app, try getting up at the same time every day, even on Sundays.
tasks.question_en: What is the host's main point?
options: Phones are the main reason people can't fall asleep
An irregular schedule matters more than screens
A good sleep app can fix an irregular schedule
Everyone should go to bed at eleven every night
tasks.explanation_ru: Ведущий признаёт, что screens do play a part, но главным называет другое: the research... points somewhere else: to irregular schedules — и советует вставать в одно и то же время каждый день. Покупать приложение он как раз не советует, а eleven — лишь пример будничного отбоя.

tasks.script_en:
Hannah: Hi, my suitcase didn't come out on the belt. I just flew in from Atlanta.
Oscar: Sorry about that. Can I see your baggage tag? OK, it looks like it's still in Atlanta. It'll be on the next flight, which lands at, uh, nine tonight. No, nine fifteen.
Hannah: So do I have to come back and pick it up?
Oscar: No. Once it lands, we'll scan it here, and then a courier will take it to your hotel, probably before midnight. Just fill out this form with your address before you leave.
Hannah: Great, thanks so much.
tasks.question_en: What will happen right after the suitcase is scanned?
options: Hannah will pick it up at the airport
A courier will take it to her hotel
It will be put on the next flight
Hannah will fill out a form
tasks.explanation_ru: Порядок: чемодан прилетит следующим рейсом (в 21:15) → we'll scan it here → and then a courier will take it to your hotel. Форму Ханна заполняет сейчас, до ухода из аэропорта, а возвращаться за багажом ей не нужно.

tasks.script_en:
Laura: So, how was Jamie's first swim meet?
Chris: Well, he came in last in both races. Actually, no, second to last in the relay.
Laura: Oh no. Was he upset?
Chris: That's the funny thing. He talked about it the whole way home: the starting blocks, the big timing boards, the older kids' dives. Then he asked if we could go to the pool on Saturday so he could practice his turns.
Laura: Sounds like you'll be spending a lot of weekends at the pool.
tasks.question_en: What can be inferred about Jamie?
options: He wants to quit swimming after losing
He's excited about swimming despite losing
He won one of his two races
He only enjoyed watching the older kids
tasks.explanation_ru: Прямо это не сказано, но после проигрыша Джейми всю дорогу говорил о соревнованиях (talked about it the whole way home) и сам попросился в субботу в бассейн, чтобы practice his turns, — плавание его увлекло. Он ничего не выиграл: last и second to last.

tasks.script_en: So I finally called customer service about the broken blender. And I'll give them this: the woman I spoke to was lovely, really apologetic. But it took forty, no, closer to fifty minutes on hold just to reach her, and then she told me I'd have to mail it back at my own cost. For a blender that's two weeks old! I mean, I'll probably get my money back eventually, but I'm not buying anything from that company again.
tasks.question_en: How does the speaker feel about the company?
options: Satisfied, because the agent was so helpful
Frustrated, even though the agent was kind
Angry with the agent, but happy with the company
Worried that the money won't be refunded
tasks.explanation_ru: Сотрудницу говорящий хвалит (lovely, really apologetic), но почти пятьдесят минут ожидания и пересылка за свой счёт его злят, и вывод такой: I'm not buying anything from that company again. Деньги он, скорее всего, вернёт — probably get my money back eventually.

tasks.script_en: The shorter signup form increased completed registrations by nine percent, which looks encouraging at first glance. However, the improvement came almost entirely from mobile visitors. Desktop conversion remained unchanged, and the number of people who verified their email actually fell by two percent. We should keep the form but test a clearer verification screen before declaring the experiment successful.
tasks.question_en: Which metric became worse during the experiment?
options: Mobile registrations
Desktop conversion
Email verification
Completed registrations overall
tasks.explanation_ru: Общие регистрации выросли, desktop не изменился, а число подтвердивших email снизилось на 2 % (fell by two percent).

tasks.script_en: A separate service would give the reporting team independent releases and clearer ownership. It would also introduce another database, deployment pipeline, and on-call responsibility for a component that currently handles modest traffic. Rather than splitting it out now, I suggest defining a strict internal interface and measuring whether the existing module becomes a genuine bottleneck over the next quarter.
tasks.question_en: What is the speaker recommending?
options: Creating a separate service right away
Splitting it out next quarter, whatever the data shows
Keeping the module but giving it its own database
Keeping it for now and watching for a bottleneck
tasks.explanation_ru: Отдельный сервис дал бы независимые релизы, но добавил бы базу, pipeline и дежурства. Поэтому говорящий предлагает пока не выделять модуль: задать строгий интерфейс и в течение квартала измерять, станет ли он настоящим bottleneck. Разделения через квартал он не обещает — всё решат измерения.

tasks.script_en: Confirm that the alert reflects customer impact rather than a monitoring fault. If it does, appoint an incident lead and open the shared timeline before paging the database team. Notify senior management only after the lead has published an initial impact estimate, unless legal or security concerns require immediate escalation.
tasks.question_en: Normally, what must happen before senior management is notified?
options: Legal or security approves the escalation
The lead publishes an impact estimate
The database team fixes the problem
The monitoring fault is repaired
tasks.explanation_ru: В обычном случае руководство уведомляют only after the lead has published an initial impact estimate. Legal и security — не согласование, а повод эскалировать сразу; ждать исправления проблемы не нужно, а monitoring fault — как раз случай, когда эскалации нет.

tasks.script_en: Dana normally challenges every estimate in the planning meeting, but today she accepted the six-week proposal without a single question. She had just come from a budget review, and afterward she asked me which features depend on the contractors' code and who else on the team could maintain it.
tasks.question_en: What is Dana probably expecting?
options: The project is about to get extra funding
The contractors may soon leave the project
The contractors' code will have to be rewritten
The team will soon hire more full-time engineers
tasks.explanation_ru: Dana пришла с budget review и спрашивает, какие функции держатся на коде подрядчиков и кто ещё в команде сможет его поддерживать, — она готовится к тому, что contractors уйдут. О новых деньгах, найме или переписывании кода в записи ничего нет.

tasks.script_en: I appreciate the attempt to make collaboration more deliberate, and two shared office days could help new employees build relationships. What worries me is the blanket requirement for everyone, regardless of role, location, or team performance. A policy with explicit exceptions and a review after three months would be far easier to support.
tasks.question_en: Which description best matches the speaker's position?
options: Supports the rule but wants more office days
Supports the goal but objects to one rule for everyone
Supports the goal but wants the rule for new hires only
Accepts the rule but doubts it will help collaboration
tasks.explanation_ru: Цель (more deliberate collaboration) и два общих дня говорящий принимает, но возражает против blanket requirement for everyone и просит явные исключения и пересмотр через три месяца. Новичков он упоминает как тех, кому общие дни помогут, а не как единственных, для кого нужно правило.

tasks.script_en:
Grace: Your first novel came out when you were in your fifties, so people tend to assume it took you decades to write.
Martin: Ha, they do. The truth is, I carried the idea around for about twenty years, but the actual writing took just under three. No, let me be honest, closer to four, if you count the rewrite my editor insisted on.
Grace: The rewrite being the new ending?
Martin: Right. In the original, the brother survives. My editor said, you know, the book had earned something darker, and she was right, annoyingly.
Grace: And the sequel?
Martin: Half-drafted. Don't hold your breath.
tasks.question_en: Including the rewrite, how long did the actual writing take?
options: Just under three years
Close to four years
About twenty years
Several decades
tasks.explanation_ru: Мартин сначала говорит just under three, но сразу поправляется: closer to four, if you count the rewrite. Twenty years он носил идею в голове, а decades — предположение публики, которое он опровергает.

tasks.script_en: In a vote late last night, the city council approved a plan that will, in effect, end single-family-only zoning across most of the city. Supporters argue that allowing duplexes and small apartment buildings on ordinary residential lots is the fastest way to bring rents down, or, well, at least to slow their rise. Opponents, many of them longtime homeowners, say the change was rushed and will put pressure on parking and schools. The plan doesn't take effect until January, and the council has promised to review its impact on traffic after the first year. Meanwhile, a petition to put the decision to a public vote is already circulating.
tasks.question_en: What is the report mainly about?
options: A new city rule that caps rents in apartment buildings
A council vote allowing more housing on residential lots
A homeowners' petition against new schools and parking
A study of how the new zoning has affected traffic
tasks.explanation_ru: Главное — решение совета: approved a plan that will... end single-family-only zoning, то есть на обычных участках разрешат дуплексы и небольшие дома. Снижение аренды — лишь надежда сторонников, петиция пока только собирает подписи, а влияние на трафик обещали изучить через год.

tasks.script_en:
Nora: So the train strike's confirmed for Tuesday. What does that do to our plan?
Adam: Well, we can't get to the coast on Tuesday, so let's flip it. We'll do the wine country first and pick up the rental car on Monday afternoon instead of Wednesday.
Nora: And drop it off where?
Adam: Back in the city, Wednesday night. Then Thursday morning we take the train to the coast, assuming the strike's over by then.
Nora: And if it isn't?
Adam: Then we just keep the car an extra day and drive. Oh, and first thing tomorrow we need to move the coast hotel from Tuesday to Thursday, before the prices jump.
tasks.question_en: Under the new plan, what will they do right after returning the car?
options: Drive out to the wine country
Take the train to the coast
Keep the car for an extra day
Move the coast hotel booking
tasks.explanation_ru: Новый порядок: в понедельник взять машину → винодельческий край → вернуть её в городе в среду вечером → Then Thursday morning we take the train to the coast. Лишний день с машиной — лишь запасной вариант, если забастовка не кончится, а отель переносят first thing tomorrow, ещё до поездки.

tasks.script_en: Hey, it's me. So I talked to Dad this afternoon. He says he's fine, and, you know, he probably is, mostly. But he asked me twice, maybe three times, what day it was, and when I mentioned his doctor's appointment, he said he'd never heard of it, even though he's the one who booked it. The fridge was nearly empty, too, which isn't like him at all. I don't want to make a big deal out of it, but maybe we should talk this weekend about, well, how often one of us drops by. Anyway, call me back when you can.
tasks.question_en: What is the caller most likely worried about?
options: Dad has stopped taking his medicine
Dad is struggling to manage on his own
Dad has argued with his doctor
Dad can no longer afford groceries
tasks.explanation_ru: Прямо об этом не сказано, но отец несколько раз спрашивает, какой сегодня день, не помнит о приёме, который сам записал, а холодильник почти пустой (which isn't like him). Поэтому звонящий предлагает обсудить, how often one of us drops by, — отцу, похоже, уже трудно справляться одному. О лекарствах, ссоре с врачом или деньгах речи нет.

tasks.script_en:
Ruth: So, what did you make of it? You were very quiet at intermission.
Leon: I was trying to work out whether I liked it. The staging was extraordinary: that revolving set, the lighting in the second act.
Ruth: But?
Leon: But I never once cared what happened to anyone. It's as if the director was so pleased with the machinery that the actors became, well, furniture. Technically brilliant, emotionally, I'd say hollow. No, that's harsh. Cold.
Ruth: I'd have said the same about the first half, honestly, but the ending really got me.
Leon: See, by then I was checking my watch.
tasks.question_en: What is Leon's opinion of the play?
options: He admired the staging but found it emotionally cold
He was bored in the first half but loved the ending
He disliked the set but thought the acting was strong
He found it moving but too long and too technical
tasks.explanation_ru: Постановку Леон хвалит (The staging was extraordinary), но ему ни разу не было дела до героев: I never once cared what happened to anyone, — и смягчает hollow до Cold. Финал понравился Рут, а Леон к тому времени смотрел на часы.

tasks.script_en: The headline forecast puts annual growth at seven percent, but that figure assumes the enterprise contract closes in September and is recognized immediately. Under the finance team's more conservative scenario, where revenue is spread across the contract term, reported growth would be closer to four and a half percent. Neither estimate includes a possible acquisition, despite recent speculation in the press.
tasks.question_en: Why could the seven percent headline figure be misleading?
options: It counts all the contract's revenue at once
It already includes the possible acquisition
It assumes the contract will not close until next year
It is based on the finance team's cautious method
tasks.explanation_ru: Seven percent предполагает, что enterprise contract закроют в сентябре и выручку признают сразу (recognized immediately). Консервативный сценарий финансистов распределяет её по сроку контракта и даёт около 4,5 %, а возможная покупка компании не входит ни в один прогноз.

tasks.script_en: Allowing each team to choose its own tools has encouraged experimentation, but it has also left the company maintaining five deployment systems and training engineers repeatedly on local conventions. A central platform must not become a gatekeeper that freezes good ideas. Its mandate should be to provide a well-supported default and transparent extension points, while requiring exceptions to carry their own operational costs.
tasks.question_en: What is the speaker's main proposal?
options: Let the central platform approve new tools before any team adopts them
Keep a supported default, but let teams opt out at their own cost
Keep full team choice, with the platform paying to run every exception
Move every team to one deployment system with a single set of conventions
tasks.explanation_ru: Говорящий предлагает поддерживаемый default с extension points; исключения допустимы, но сами несут свои эксплуатационные расходы. Роль привратника он прямо отвергает (must not become a gatekeeper), а переводить всех на одну систему не требует.

tasks.script_en: Do not lead with the discount, because that would make price the only reference point. First establish which service guarantees the client genuinely values, then quantify what meeting them costs us. Once the client acknowledges that trade-off, offer the longer contract in exchange for the lower rate. Leave the termination clause until last, after the commercial terms are provisionally settled.
tasks.question_en: When should the lower rate be offered?
options: At the very start
After the client accepts the service-cost trade-off
Only after the termination clause is signed
Before discussing service guarantees
tasks.explanation_ru: Сначала ценность гарантий и их стоимость, затем признание trade-off, и только после этого lower rate за длинный контракт.

tasks.script_en: The board praised the proposal's ambition and asked the team to refine the implementation timeline. At the same time, it postponed the funding decision, requested a scenario requiring half the initial capital, and added the chief risk officer to every future review. No one rejected the strategy outright, but the next presentation has been reduced from an hour to twenty minutes.
tasks.question_en: What can most reasonably be inferred about the board?
options: It is ready to fund the plan once the timeline is refined
It is interested but not ready to commit the full budget
It thinks the proposal is not ambitious enough
It wants a longer, more detailed presentation next time
tasks.explanation_ru: Интерес есть: совет похвалил ambition, просит уточнить timeline, и стратегию никто не отверг. Но решение о деньгах отложено (postponed the funding decision), нужен сценарий с половиной initial capital, а в каждый review добавлен chief risk officer — всю сумму совет давать пока не готов. Амбициозность он как раз хвалит, а следующую презентацию не удлинил, а сократил с часа до двадцати минут.

tasks.script_en: Leadership describes the reorganization as a way to eliminate duplication, which is a legitimate concern. Yet the published chart moves decision-making upward while leaving delivery targets untouched, and the consultation period begins only after the new roles have been announced. Calling that empowerment stretches the word beyond recognition. I would support consolidation if authority moved closer to the teams actually carrying the risk.
tasks.question_en: What is the speaker's attitude toward the reorganization?
options: Accepts the aim but objects to decisions moving upward
Welcomes the new roles but wishes consultation had started earlier
Doubts that duplication exists but likes the new chart
Accepts the new chart but wants lower delivery targets
tasks.explanation_ru: Цель убрать duplication говорящий называет legitimate concern, но критикует то, что решения уходят наверх (moves decision-making upward), и поддержит консолидацию, только если authority moved closer to the teams. Позднюю consultation он приводит как ещё один симптом, а новые роли и схему не одобряет.

tasks.script_en: And finally, a story that's been, shall we say, a little overhyped. You may have seen headlines claiming that a daily walk cuts your risk of dementia in half. The study behind them is real, and fairly large: about twelve thousand adults, well, twelve and a half thousand, followed for nine years. But what it actually found is that people who walked roughly forty minutes a day had a risk about a third lower than those who barely walked at all. Not half. A third. And that's an association, not proof of cause, since people in the early stages of decline may simply walk less. The authors themselves are careful on this point; it's the press releases that weren't. None of which, of course, is a reason to stay on the couch.
tasks.question_en: According to the study, how much lower was the risk for people who walked about forty minutes a day?
options: About half
About a third
About forty percent
About twelve percent
tasks.explanation_ru: Заголовки обещали in half, но ведущий уточняет: a risk about a third lower... Not half. A third. Forty — это минуты ходьбы в день, а twelve — тысячи участников исследования.

tasks.script_en:
Julia: Your city's introduced a daily fee for day-trippers. Critics are calling it a tax on curiosity. Is that fair?
Marco: It's a good line, I'll give them that. But the fee isn't really about revenue; it barely covers the cost of collecting it. The point is to spread visitors out. On a peak Saturday we get, what, eighty thousand people, some days closer to ninety, in a historic center built for maybe a tenth of that.
Julia: So you're pricing people out.
Marco: We're pricing people into Tuesday. The fee only applies on about thirty peak days, and it's waived for anyone staying overnight, because those visitors actually sustain local businesses rather than just, you know, passing through.
Julia: And if it doesn't work?
Marco: Then we've learned something cheaply, and we'll drop it.
tasks.question_en: What is Marco's main argument?
options: The fee mainly raises money to protect the historic center
The fee is meant to spread visits out, not to raise money
The fee is meant to keep day-trippers away from the city
The fee should also apply to visitors who stay overnight
tasks.explanation_ru: Марко прямо отделяет сбор от дохода (isn't really about revenue) и называет цель: to spread visitors out — We're pricing people into Tuesday, то есть переносит поездки на спокойные дни. Отпугивать туристов вообще он не хочет, а для тех, кто ночует в городе, сбор отменён (waived).

tasks.script_en: Hi, it's Deborah from Lane Realty, following up on the sale. So, the buyers' lender has, finally, signed off on the appraisal, which means we can move forward, but the order really matters here. Before anything gets scheduled, I need the signed disclosure form back; I can't release the draft contract without it. Once the buyers have reviewed that draft, their inspector wants one more visit. The whole house again, no, sorry, just the roof. Assuming nothing new turns up, we'll book the closing, and you hand over the keys at the closing itself, not before, whatever their agent suggests. Oh, and please don't cancel your home insurance until the funds have actually cleared. Call me if any of that's unclear.
tasks.question_en: What must happen immediately before the roof inspection?
options: The seller returns the signed disclosure form
The buyers review the draft contract
The seller hands over the keys
The closing date is booked
tasks.explanation_ru: Цепочка такая: подписанная disclosure form → черновик договора → Once the buyers have reviewed that draft, their inspector wants one more visit → closing и передача ключей прямо на нём. Непосредственно перед осмотром крыши покупатели изучают черновик; форма нужна раньше, а closing и ключи — позже.

tasks.script_en:
Kevin: Coach, you took Marcus Sanchez off at halftime. Is he injured?
Diane: No, he's fine. Fully fit.
Kevin: Then why bench him in a game you needed to win?
Diane: Look, we have to think beyond tonight. The young guys need minutes, and, frankly, they need to learn to win without leaning on one player.
Kevin: There've been reports of offers from Europe. Any truth to that?
Diane: I'm not going to comment on rumors. What I will say is that Marcus has given this club seven great years, eight, actually, if you count the youth team, and whatever happens this summer, people here will remember that.
Kevin: That sounds a lot like a goodbye.
Diane: It's a thank-you. Next question.
tasks.question_en: What do the coach's answers suggest?
options: Sanchez is hiding an injury from the press
Sanchez will leave the club soon
The coach is unhappy with how Sanchez played
The young players will be sold this summer
tasks.explanation_ru: Прямо тренер ничего не подтверждает, но подводит итог годам Маркуса в клубе (has given this club seven great years), добавляет whatever happens this summer и заранее учит молодых выигрывать without leaning on one player — всё это похоже на подготовку к его уходу. Травму она отрицает (Fully fit), а претензий к его игре не высказывает.

tasks.script_en: I'll admit I went in expecting to hate it. A three-hour documentary about, of all things, a public library sounded like a punishment. And the first hour does test your patience: no narration, no music, just meetings about budgets. But somewhere in the second hour, I realized I'd stopped checking the time. Watching a librarian spend twenty minutes helping an elderly man fill out a benefits form is more moving than most thrillers manage. Is it too long? Probably, yes, by about forty minutes, maybe even an hour. Would I sit through it again? Honestly, I'm not sure I would. But I'm glad I saw it once, and I've been recommending it to, well, my more patient friends.
tasks.question_en: What is the speaker's overall attitude toward the documentary?
options: Bored by it and sorry to have gone
Won over by it, despite finding it too long
Eager to see it again as soon as possible
Moved mostly by the meetings about budgets
tasks.explanation_ru: Говорящий шёл с мыслью, что фильм ему не понравится (expecting to hate it), и признаёт, что он too long, но со второго часа перестал смотреть на часы, называет эпизод с библиотекарем more moving than most thrillers и рад, что посмотрел. Пересматривать он не уверен (I'm not sure I would), а встречи о бюджетах — как раз скучная часть.
